stories.title: Internet Cables Fixed After Bishan-Thomson Blackout
stories.headline_kid: Construction workers accidentally cut internet cables in Bishan and Thomson, but everything is fixed now!
summary: On Tuesday, workers doing road-widening in Bishan and Thomson accidentally damaged underground fibre cables. These cables are like the pipes that carry internet signals to our homes.
About 2,000 homes and offices lost their internet connection because of this. The cables belong to a company called NetLink Trust, which supplies internet lines to Singtel, StarHub and M1.
Engineers worked through the night to repair the damage. By 5.40am on Wednesday, all the affected connections were working again.
This shows how much we rely on the internet every day — for online homework, video calls with relatives, and even watching cartoons. When it suddenly disappears, we realise just how important it is!

lenses.me: If your home's Wi-Fi ever stops working, it might be because of damaged cables underground, not your device.
lenses.family: Families in Bishan and Thomson could not go online for schoolwork or bills for almost a day.
lenses.friends: Classmates living in those areas may have missed online homework portals or video calls with friends.
lenses.nation: Singapore's internet network is usually very reliable, so a breakdown like this is unusual and gets fixed fast.
lenses.world: Countries everywhere depend on underground cables for internet — accidents like this can happen anywhere construction work takes place.

stories.title: Thailand and Cambodia Argue Their Case in Singapore
stories.headline_kid: Thailand and Cambodia are having a big disagreement over their shared border, and they brought it to Singapore to be sorted out fairly.
summary: Thailand and Cambodia have been arguing for a long time about land along the border they share. To solve this peacefully, both countries agreed to bring their dispute to a special court called the Permanent Court of Arbitration, which is meeting in Singapore.
On Tuesday, Thailand's foreign minister spoke in front of judges. He accused Cambodia of spreading untrue stories and unfairly blaming Thailand, calling it 'playing the victim'.
This meeting is called a conciliation commission. Think of it like a trusted teacher stepping in to help two arguing classmates talk things through calmly, instead of letting the argument get worse.
Singapore was chosen to host these talks because it is seen as fair and neutral. This shows how much other countries trust Singapore to help solve big problems peacefully.

lenses.me: It's a good example of how grown-ups and countries can be encouraged to solve arguments with words instead of fighting.
lenses.family: Your family might discuss this if they follow the news about Thailand and Cambodia's relationship.
lenses.friends: You could talk to friends about how disagreements, even big ones between countries, can be settled through calm discussion.
lenses.nation: Singapore's reputation as a trusted, neutral meeting place is strengthened whenever it hosts important international talks like this.
lenses.world: A peaceful resolution helps keep the whole Southeast Asian region stable and safe for everyone.

stories.title: Haze Gets Worse Across Malaysia, Singapore Keeps Watch
stories.headline_kid: Smoky haze is spreading across Malaysia, and hot dry weather means it might not clear up soon.
summary: Haze happens when smoke from fires — often from land being cleared by burning — fills the air and makes it hazy and hard to breathe. Right now, Malaysia is dealing with a bad bout of haze.
On Tuesday, 38 areas across Malaysia recorded 'unhealthy' air quality. Sarawak, especially the town of Serian, had the worst readings, while Johor had the most affected areas.
The hot, dry weather isn't just making the haze worse — it's also causing rivers and water sources in Sarawak to drop to low levels, which worries residents who depend on that water.
Experts say this dry spell could continue into next month. Since haze can drift with the wind, Singapore keeps a close eye on our own air quality (called the PSI) too, in case it affects us.

lenses.me: If the haze reaches Singapore, you might need to stay indoors during recess or PE instead of playing outside.
lenses.family: Families may need to keep windows closed or use air purifiers if the haze becomes bad here too.
lenses.friends: Outdoor activities like sports day or excursions could be cancelled if the air quality turns unhealthy.
lenses.nation: Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) monitors the PSI daily and issues advisories to keep everyone safe.
lenses.world: Haze crossing borders shows how one country's forest fires can affect the health of people in neighbouring countries too.

stories.title: Rescuers Battle Rough Seas to Find Missing Ferry Passengers
stories.headline_kid: A ferry flipped over near Indonesia, and huge waves are making it hard for rescuers to find everyone who is still missing.
summary: A passenger ferry called Virgo Transport 8 capsized, which means it flipped over, while sailing across the Java Sea from Surabaya to Banjarmasin in Indonesia.
Rescuers have managed to bring nearly two dozen survivors safely to shore. Sadly, dozens of people are still missing, and the search continues.
The weather has made the rescue extremely difficult. Indonesia's search and rescue agency said the waves and swells in the area were 'extremely high', making it dangerous even for trained rescuers.
Ferries are a very common way to travel between Indonesia's many islands. This sad event reminds everyone how important it is to check the weather and follow safety rules before sailing.

lenses.me: If your family ever travels by ferry, this reminds you why wearing a life jacket and following safety instructions matters.
lenses.family: Families with relatives or friends travelling in Indonesia may feel worried when hearing news like this.
lenses.friends: You could talk with classmates about the importance of checking weather warnings before any sea trip.
lenses.nation: Singapore, as a close neighbour, often supports Indonesia with aid or rescue help during emergencies like this.
lenses.world: This tragedy highlights the need for stronger ferry safety standards across the whole region.

stories.title: Singapore Student Invents Clever All-in-One Milk Bottle
stories.headline_kid: A 23-year-old NUS graduate designed a smart invention to make feeding breast milk easier for parents on the go — and won a top design award!
summary: Nicolette Wong, a 23-year-old graduate of the National University of Singapore, noticed that her sister struggled with feeding breast milk while out and about. Parents often had to carry separate items — one to store milk, another to warm it, and another to feed it — which was troublesome.
So Nicolette designed Momigo, a clever all-in-one system. It lets parents store, warm and feed breast milk using just one single container, instead of juggling many different products.
Her invention won the Singapore title in the James Dyson Award 2026, a well-known global competition that celebrates young inventors and designers who solve everyday problems.
This story shows how a school project — she designed Momigo as her final-year thesis — can turn into a real invention that could help parents everywhere feed their babies more easily.

lenses.me: It shows that even a school project can become something useful and impressive if you notice a real problem around you.
lenses.family: Parents at home, especially those with babies, might find an invention like Momigo very helpful during outings.
lenses.friends: You and your classmates could be inspired to think of your own inventions for problems you notice in daily life.
lenses.nation: Singapore is proud to have young inventors like Nicolette representing the country in global design competitions.
lenses.world: Her invention could eventually help parents around the world feed their babies more conveniently.

compo_words.example: Her innovative design combined three tools into one.
